messages:
morgan: FYI — ACME (tenant 98123) reports ~2k audit entries missing from the S3 export after our KMS key rotation at 2026-02-18T11:10Z. SIEM shows a clear gap 11:12–11:20 UTC. Forwarder logs have repeated `DecryptRequestDenied` entries for a subset of objects. Can someone triage?

devon: Can you paste the object keys/prefix and an example error from the forwarder logs? Also which alias was rotated?

morgan: prefix: `audit/tenant=98123/date=2026-02-18/` — sample forwarder log: ```ERROR 2026-02-18T11:15:03Z ForwarderWorker DecryptRequestDenied: KeyAliasMismatch: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:alias/redwood-audit-v1 not found for ciphertext```. Rotation was to `alias/redwood-audit-v2` at 11:10Z.

ashley: Two quick hypotheses: 1) some manifests still reference the old alias (we saw eventual-consistency when aliases switch), 2) the forwarder process caches the KMS key id/ARN on startup and didn't reload the new alias -> skipped decrypts and moved objects to dead-letter.

ashley: Repro steps I used locally to reproduce the `DecryptRequestDenied` error: ```# emulate forwarder decrypt
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-staging/audit/tenant=98123/date=2026-02-18/sample.enc ./
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://sample.enc --region us-east-1 --key-id alias/redwood-audit-v1
# returns KeyAliasMismatch when alias was removed```

secops-bot: Incident INC-4822 created and linked: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4822 — severity: P1 — owner: devon. Playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/audit-export-backfill

devon: I'll take this. First steps: 1) validate S3 object ACLs + manifest entries for tenant 98123, 2) check forwarder process env for cached KMS ARN, 3) check DLQ for the skipped objects and list ciphertexts. If DLQ has ciphertexts, we can re-encrypt/replay.

morgan: DLQ count ~2,034 objects. We shouldn't re-ingest before PB approval. Customer is requesting visibility and a replay.

ashley: Quick check I ran — IAM logs show the forwarder used role `redwood-forwarder-prod` and succeeded for most objects, but there are ~2k entries where `kms:Decrypt` was denied because the request specified an old key-id. The manifest-generation job writes key metadata into the manifest; if that wasn't updated atomically with alias rotation the forwarder will try the old id.

ashley: Proposed remediation: short-term: run a replay that sets `--ignore-key-id` to let the forwarder ask KMS by alias instead of manifest key-id (this is supported by the backfill tool). Long-term: change manifest writer to store alias only and add a small alias-consistency check on rotation.

devon: Commands I'll run (sandbox first): ```# list DLQ objects
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-forwarder-dlq/tenant=98123/ --recursive | wc -l
# backfill replay (sandbox)
redwood-backfill --tenant 98123 --start 2026-02-18T11:10 --end 2026-02-18T11:25 --mode replay --ignore-key-id --dry-run
```

morgan: Please keep acct team posted. Can we also confirm retention/visibility metrics — customer wants assurance no events were dropped permanently (they need retention proof for compliance).

ashley: I'll export the DLQ object list + attempted decrypt errors and attach to the incident. If replay succeeds, we record a signed re-ingest audit event. If any objects are corrupted, we'll surface to legal/compliance.

devon: Action plan: 1) run dry-run replay (in 15m), 2) if dry-run clean, schedule live replay with customer notification and a 1h maintenance window, 3) patch manifest-writer to prefer alias and add guard for rotation. I'll post logs back here.

morgan: thanks — marking P1, assigning to devon/ashley. Please @pager if you need extra hands. :thumbsup:
